Operator confirmed rover is in Dhruv Room, not whether it occupies the exact saved home point. Live AMCL pose (-3.17,-0.22) is 3.67 m from named Dhruv Room pose (0.254,-1.539). Saved Oct8 seed (0.877,0.097) has no accepted-map ID. Localization service showed six start-preflight timeout restarts concurrent with repeated LiDAR hardware operation timeouts; missing scans are the likely immediate cause, not a demonstrated seed failure. Once running, Nav2 logs contained robot-out-of-map positions and one scan/TF cache drop. No motion or runtime change. Exact faulty coordinate source remains unproven.

Exact accepted PGM lookup put later live pose (-3.22,-0.25) in unknown 205 cells, while the saved Dhruv Room point was known free 254. A stopped 15-second diagnostic recorded fresh scans, zero wheel/EKF odometry drift and 0.004 m/1.09 degree AMCL drift. Added a saved-map known-clear start check before named-place and return-home goal dispatch; offline regression passed. Physical localization and room-route reliability remain unvalidated.

Operator confirmed exact saved Dhruv Room position and heading. Fresh LiDAR scan endpoints fit that map pose far better than the old out-of-map AMCL pose. Backed up the old localization seed and invoked the existing AMCL seed service once while stopped. Post-seed authoritative pose was about 9 cm from home, in known free space; 99% of fresh scan endpoints were within 15 cm of mapped walls, with motor speed zero. This does not qualify moving or reboot repeatability, the Hall endpoint, or the saved taught route.

Operator manually arrived in Hall and confirmed live map marker. Fresh stopped scan fit 98.9% within 15 cm at (6.279,-2.199); exact accepted-map 0.18 m clearance and grid connectivity to home passed. Old Hall waypoint was backed up. First save was incorrectly bound to an Oct8 mapping session left active while localization ran and SLAM was inactive; archived the stale marker and re-saved Hall with accepted map ID. Motor speed remained zero during save. Manual arrival was not captured by the dedicated demonstration recorder; taught-route map ID and autonomous repeatability remain unvalidated.

Dedicated Hall-to-Dhruv manual return bag captured fresh scan, odom, TF and AMCL. Remote-command interval had no >2 s data gap, but five AMCL steps exceeded 0.5 m after the remote stopped and odometry was stationary; largest was 2.206 m/130 degrees. The 4.236 m wheel-odom endpoint displacement does not prove distance under-reporting because its recorded path length was about 6.77 m. Of 65 unavailable encoder samples, 32 occurred with traction and CRITICAL/autonomy_ready=false health. Wheel-derived yaw-rate integration was about -143 degrees versus about -192 degrees from IM10A/EKF. Browser map refresh was bounded and stale data labelled, but root localization reliability remains unproven. No autonomous motion was commanded.

Offline replay in isolated ROS domain 178 changed only wheel X/Y pose fusion. Across 31 Hall-anchored scans, median saved-map endpoint fit within 15 cm improved from 23.1% to 50.2% with velocity-only wheel input; last-10-second fit improved from 11.1% to 52.2%. The earlier Oct8 replay was mixed and this candidate still underfits, so production EKF/Nav2 remains unchanged. Read-only web map now displays AMCL covariance and recent jumps; replay classifier flagged all five post-stop corrections, and the deployed API/page returned HTTP 200. No motor or autonomous command was issued.

Eleven relevant wheel/corrected-IMU/scan bags inventoried; only Hall return had enough AMCL data for jump counts. Encoder-selection replay matched recorded updates exactly, including wrong-sign wheel yaw versus gyro/scan ICP with four accepted wheels. Isolated saved-map AMCL replay produced 0 >0.5 m jumps in both variants and therefore did not reproduce five live jumps; velocity-only reduced maximum correction but worsened final ~20 s AMCL position span from 0.845 m to 1.789 m. Production EKF/Nav2 unchanged; localization unresolved.

Read-only commanded-steering sensitivity: the Oct9 4.35 s wrong-sign interval remained +7.42/+4.27/+2.43/+1.30 degrees at 0/0.2/0.5/0.75 s delay, versus corrected gyro -18.96 and scan ICP -16.09 degrees. Another turn worsened with 0.5 s delay. Scan transport beyond acquisition and TF consistency did not reveal a seconds-long data gap at the largest post-stop AMCL correction. Physical road-wheel angle remains unmeasured; no parameter changed.

Live rover-base-telemetry executes the repository-matching Yahboom driver; steering writes PWM channels 2/1 with no external position readback. Vendor get_uart_servo_angle belongs to a different bus-servo interface; retired ST3215 configuration is not live. Wheel odometry uses commanded servo offsets as road-wheel angles before encoder normalization and for yaw/X/Y. Physical servo model, shaft position, linkage angle and traction remain unmeasured. No safe model or EKF correction identified; autonomous gate remains closed.

Read-only per-event Hall-return audit: all five 0.565-2.206 m AMCL steps occurred 2.856-13.063 s after the last remote command. Nearby wheel XY change and corrected gyro turn were zero, with 6-8 LiDAR scans between each pair and AMCL XY standard deviation already >1 m. These are stationary localization-hypothesis switches, not physical motion at jump times. Operator photos show satisfactory visible steering response but do not measure actual wheel angles; steering config preserved. Upstream heading disagreement versus scan/map ambiguity remains unresolved; no production tuning or motion.

Continued from 54e6519 using the existing Hall-return bag. Five AMCL steps had fresh pre-event LiDAR scans (receipt age 11-34 ms), particle clouds (age 0-3 ms), zero/near-zero odometry step, and XY uncertainty 1.14-1.39 m. Spatially diffuse particles supported competing poses; event 4 switched back despite worsening same-scan endpoint fit from 100.0% to 86.6% within 15 cm. Approximate map-ray diagnostics are not AMCL likelihood. Beam-model saved-map replay gave 0 jumps but 2.865 m final position span with current EKF, and 1 jump of 0.657 m with velocity-only EKF; current model replayed with 0 jumps in both EKFs but did not reproduce five live jumps. No candidate validated, no production change, autonomy gated.

Continued from 99bd418. Original recorded map and saved atlas_latest.pgm matched all 51,040 trinary cells. The prior 75.918 s replay clip omitted 8 of 537 source scans and regenerated EKF odometry; original window had 759 /odom, 168 AMCL poses and 5 jumps. New isolated AMCL-only replay included all 537 scans and 759 original /odom/TF in input, but its output recorder saw 524 scans, 743 odom and 120 AMCL poses; an early scan was dropped for missing TF history. Two runs both yielded zero large jumps, max step 0.239 m and final ~19 s span 0.462 m. Original/replay median particle spread was 0.810/0.415 m. A full-bag replay also stopped outputting AMCL poses before the original jump window. A replay-only zero-motion-threshold experiment produced 512 AMCL poses and one 1.827 m correction in each of two runs, not the original five. Internal particle/RNG state, exact runtime AMCL parameters and original scheduling are not restored; no valid five-jump baseline or candidate fix. Production unchanged, autonomy gated.

Mission-control source and original Jetson journal confirm approximately 1 Hz /request_nomotion_update calls through the five-jump window, omitted by previous replays. After the last remote command, original odom and odom->base TF drifted at most 0.01221 m/0.504 degrees, below replay motion gates. A full-bag isolated localhost-domain replay sent 294 phase-matched calls with no skips; AMCL logged all 294. It matched original 384 total/80 post-stop pose counts and produced two post-stop >0.5 m jumps (max 3.470 m), versus original five (max 2.206 m). The missing service trigger explains absent earlier replay updates and reproduces stationary hypothesis switching, but not the exact live trajectory or upstream cause. No production parameter, service or actuator changed; autonomy remains gated.

Read-only same-hypothesis scan-window comparison of five live and two replay post-stop jumps. All original jumps had broad clouds with 1.137-1.384 m after-cloud XY spread; replay jumps had 1.292/1.364 m. Original jumps 1 and 4 selected poses with worse diagnostic endpoint proximity on all seven preceding scans each (57.6->51.0% and 100.0->86.3% mean within 15 cm), whereas both replay jumps improved that score on every selected scan (51.9->81.5% and 82.2->95.6%). Published weights were uniform and do not retain pre-resampling likelihood or cluster selection. These data disprove exact replay equivalence but do not identify the live AMCL scoring cause. No motion or production change.

Built pinned Nav2 AMCL 1.1.20 in a separate Jetson workspace with pre-resampling weighted-particle and selected-cluster traces. Bounded shadow instance used absolute live map/scan topics, verified tf_broadcast=false, and did not replace production AMCL or command motors. First lifecycle RPC timed out despite configuration; state verification fixed. A subsequent helper pacing bug issued 1623 shadow-only no-motion requests in 10 s and briefly raised Jetson load; corrected to monotonic 1 Hz. Accepted 10-second stationary capture sent 10 requests and recorded 7 weighted clouds, 7 shadow poses and 25 scans in an 8.10-second bag. One stable cluster was observed; no historic jump reproduced. Root cause and autonomy remain unresolved.

issues.title: Visual Cloud ingest destination is a placeholder and local history is stale
issues.original_failure_and_evidence: Active agent repeatedly logged DNS errors for atlas-visual-cloud.example. The checked-in cloud_url uses that example hostname; local history.sqlite3 was approximately 26.5 GB and last modified Oct4.
issues.confirmed_findings: Service-active status does not mean remote ingest succeeded. The server has an 86,400-row retention cap but SQLite deletion does not automatically shrink allocated pages.
issues.suspected_causes_and_limits: Exact deployment intent, current local ingest wiring and historical database growth rate have not been fully established. Database size is not evidence of a full disk; approximately 373 GB was free at the stopped-runtime check.
issues.test_results: Read-only configuration, journal, file metadata and disk checks only; no ingest repair or deployment.
issues.remaining_verification: Confirm intended authenticated endpoint and data flow; measure payload rate, retention and CPU/disk overhead. Change one existing collector only after preserving local safety and diagnostic continuity.
issues.history_completeness: Current runtime/config snapshot; older outages and remote endpoint history not exhaustively reviewed

issues.title: Failed BMS reads republish stale scalar values
issues.original_failure_and_evidence: On a Daly BLE read failure, JSON reported ok:false but publish_data emitted prior voltage/current/SOC/cells on scalar topics. The agent refreshed its SOC age from scalar percent.
issues.confirmed_findings: Scalar topics carry no validity field, so copied readings appeared new. The JSON-based motor lifted-test gate already rejected unhealthy snapshots.
issues.suspected_causes_and_limits: This is a freshness-contract defect, not proof of the underlying BLE connection cause. Other dashboard consumers may cache last values and require their own explicit stale indication.
issues.test_results: 14 focused offline Daly tests and 12 agent-core tests passed; deployed with operator approval. Short healthy-runtime check passed with unchanged motor PID, but live failure behavior and BLE endurance remain unvalidated.
issues.remaining_verification: During a natural failed BLE read, verify invalid JSON, no new scalar message, immediate agent preflight denial and successful recovery on a later complete read; complete stopped endurance observation.
issues.history_completeness: Current source and live journal reviewed; historical consumer behavior not exhaustively replayed
